ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Trajectory KL Regularization Mitigation
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of multiple variants of KL-regularized PPO with various relaxations of the trajectory KL divergence, such as using a smaller number of denoising steps in the comparison or a different aggregation scheme (e.g., using mean instead of sum to compute the KL).
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments without KL regularization, PPO with exact KL regularization, and a version of PPO with trajectory KL regularization but without the KL term (i.e., ignoring empirical stability concerns).
COST: 90000
PREDICTION: The experiments should show that using a smaller number of denoising steps or a different aggregation scheme can alleviate the instability issues associated with the exact KL regularization, but the results might still be subpar compared to other methods.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Rejection Sampling with Importance Weights for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Implement rejection sampling with importance weights for fine-tuning diffusion models, similar to RSO and RAFT but tailored to the diffusion model setting. Specifically, sample from the reference model, compute the reward for the sample, accept the sample with a probability that is a function of the reward, and use the accepted samples to train the model with a importance weighting correction.
CONTROLS: Experiments without acceptance, using rejection sampling without importance weights, and a baseline of KL-regularized PPO.
COST: 110000
PREDICTION: Rejection sampling with importance weights might improve sample quality while reducing the risk of unstable training associated with KL regularization, but the importance weights could complicate the training process, and the results might not be as effective as a more tailored approach.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Best-of-N Sampling and Policy Gradient Connection
PROPOSAL: Investigate the connection between Best-of-N sampling and policy gradient methods for fine-tuning diffusion models. Specifically, develop a theoretical framework to analyze the regret bounds of policy gradient methods for models that select high-reward samples using Best-of-N sampling. This will involve adapting existing regret bounds for policy gradient methods to the sample selection aspect of Best-of-N sampling.
CONTROLS: Theoretical analysis of Best-of-N sampling alone, in addition to its implementation as a part of policy gradient methods, and comparison to KL-regularized PPO.
COST: 125000
PREDICTION: The theoretical framework should show that policy gradient methods with Best-of-N sampling can achieve better regret bounds than KL-regularized PPO, but the results might be biased towards theoretical guarantees rather than practical performance.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Trajectory KL Regularization Mitigation
PROPOSAL: To further alleviate the instability issues associated with the exact KL regularization, explore the use of a more flexible aggregation scheme for the KL divergence, such as a weighted sum of the KL divergences of individual denoising steps. Additionally, consider a hierarchical approach where the KL regularization is applied at multiple points along the denoising path, with different weightings for each point.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments without KL regularization, and the previously proposed variants of KL-regularized PPO.
COST: 85000 -> 135000
PREDICTION: The weighted sum and hierarchical approaches should provide improved stability and flexibility in handling KL regularization, but the optimal weighting schemes and hierarchical structures might require significant tuning.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Denoising Schedule Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the idea of transferring denoising schedules learned from one domain to another while fine-tuning a diffusion model for a new task. This could be done by using a pre-trained diffusion model as a teacher to guide the fine-tuning process, with the denoising schedule used in the teacher model serving as a source of supervision.
CONTROLS: Experiments with non-transferred denoising schedules, and a baseline of fine-tuning without any pre-trained guidance.
COST: 130000
PREDICTION: The results might show that denoising schedule transfer learning can provide a performance boost, especially when the new task has a similar structure to the original task, but the tuning of the transferred denoising schedule might be challenging.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Leveraging Flow Model Structure for Fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: Develop a method that leverages the ODE structure of flow models for fine-tuning, by identifying the primary sources of the discrepancy between the pre-trained model and the target data distribution, and then modifying the ODE structure to align with these sources.
CONTROLS: Experiments with flow models fine-tuned using standard KL-regularized PPO, and a baseline of fine-tuning without modification of the ODE structure.
COST: 170000
PREDICTION: The results might show that leveraging the ODE structure can lead to improved fine-tuning performance, especially when the primary sources of discrepancy are closely related to the ODE structure, but the identification of these sources might be difficult and require significant domain expertise.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Offline Correction of Pre-trained Flow Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate a method for correcting the errors of a pre-trained flow model without explicit reward feedback, using only samples from the target data distribution. This could involve developing a loss function that measures the discrepancy between the pre-trained model and the target distribution, and then modifying the model to minimize this discrepancy.
CONTROLS: Experiments with a pre-trained flow model refined using standard KL-regularized PPO, and a baseline of no correction or separation steps
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: The results might show that offline correction can significantly improve the quality of pre-trained flow models, reducing the need for explicit reward feedback, but the method might require careful tuning of the loss function and may not be suitable for all types of errors.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Characterizing the Regret of Policy Gradient Methods for Sample Selection
PROPOSAL: Derive a regret bound for policy gradient methods used for sample selection in Best-of-N sampling. This involves analyzing the trade-off between exploration and exploitation in the sample selection process and developing a theoretical framework for understanding the regret of policy gradient methods in this context.
CONTROLS: Theoretical analysis of the regret bound for a specific policy gradient method, and comparison to the regret bounds for other methods, such as KL-regularized PPO.
COST: 200000
PREDICTION: The theoretical framework should provide a deeper understanding of the regret of policy gradient methods for sample selection, but the results might be highly dependent on the assumptions made in the regret analysis.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Text-to-Image Fine-tuning using KL-Regularized PPO with Flow Model Structure
PROPOSAL: Apply the KL-regularized PPO approach to fine-tune a pre-trained flow model for text-to-image generation tasks, leveraging the ODE structure of the flow model to regularize the KL-divergence. Evaluate the performance of this approach on standard benchmarks for text-to-image generation.
CONTROLS: Experiments with standard KL-regularized PPO, and a baseline of fine-tuning without leveraging the flow model structure.
COST: 220000
PREDICTION: The results might show that leveraging the flow model structure can lead to improved fine-tuning performance for text-to-image generation tasks, but the approach might require careful tuning of the KL-regularization term and the flow model structure.

ACTION: ADD 9
TITLE: Dataset and Application Study of Molecule Generation using Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Apply the various fine-tuning approaches proposed in this study to a pre-trained diffusion model for molecule generation tasks, and evaluate the performance of these approaches on standard benchmarks for molecule generation. Investigate how the different fine-tuning approaches affect the quality and diversity of generated molecules.
CONTROLS: Experiments with standard KL-regularized PPO, and a baseline of fine-tuning without leveraging the diffusion model structure or other proposed approaches.
COST: 250000
PREDICTION: The results might show that the fine-tuning approaches proposed in this study can lead to improved performance for molecule generation tasks, but the approach might require careful tuning of the fine-tuning loss and might not be suitable for all types of molecule generation tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating KL-Regularized Reward Maximization for Diffusion Models with Trajectory KL Constraints
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experiment using the DDM-Snet diffusion model, fine-tuning it on the ImageNet32 dataset with a KL-regularized reward maximization objective, using the trajectory KL constraint to upper-bound the intractable marginal KL divergence. We will compare the results against the baseline of ignoring the KL term and against a model fine-tuned with a relaxed KL divergence, computed between entire denoising trajectories.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of KL regularization strength
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: We expect that using the trajectory KL constraint will lead to more stable training and better fine-tuning results compared to ignoring the KL term, but at the cost of reduced performance compared to the baseline KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories. However, this could fail if the learned initial value function bias problem is too severe for the trajectory KL constraint to mitigate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Effect of the Learned Initial Value Function Bias on KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experiment using the DDM-Snet diffusion model, fine-tuning it on the ImageNet32 dataset with a KL-regularized reward maximization objective, using the trajectory KL constraint to upper-bound the intractable marginal KL divergence. We will investigate the effect of the learned initial value function bias on the fine-tuning results, by analyzing the learned reverse process and calculating the expected reward under the reference distribution, as a function of the learned noise sequences.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of KL regularization strength
- Ablation: analyzing learned reverse process for different numbers of coarse tuning iterations 
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: We expect that the learned initial value function bias will indeed be a significant issue for KL-regularized reward maximization, and that the results will show a strong dependence on the coarse tuning iterations. However, this could fail if the learned reverse process is too complex and difficult to analyze, making the quantitative investigation of the initial value bias problem infeasible.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploiting the Multi-Step Generative Structure of Diffusion Models with Variance-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will extend the KL-regularized reward maximization objective for diffusion models to include a variance-regularized term, designed to exploit the multi-step generative structure of diffusion and flow models. This will be achieved by adding a loss term that encourages the KL-regularized distribution to have a smaller variance in the noise sequences. We will conduct an experiment using the DDPM diffusion model, fine-tuning it on the CIFAR10 dataset with the variance-regularized reward maximization objective.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of KL regularization strength
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of variance regularization strength
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We expect that the variance-regularized reward maximization objective will lead to more stable training and better fine-tuning results, especially in the early stages of fine-tuning. However, this could fail if the variance regularization is too aggressive, causing the model to over-smoothen the noise sequences and lose the ability to capture the variability of the target data distribution.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Exploiting the Multi-Step Generative Structure of Diffusion Models with Variance-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will revise the previous proposal to also incorporate a forward.process KL regularization term, designed to encourage the forward noise process to be close to the denoising diffusion process. This will be achieved by adding a loss term that computes the KL divergence between the forward noise process and the denoising diffusion process. Additionally, we will also investigate the effect of co-regularizing both the forward and reverse processes. We will continue to conduct the experiment using the DDPM diffusion model, fine-tuning it on the CIFAR10 dataset with the revised variance-regularized reward maximization objective that includes the forward.process KL regularization term.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of KL regularization strength
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of variance regularization strength
- Ablation: comparing results with different co-regularization regimes for forward and reverse processes
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: We expect that co-regularizing both the forward and reverse processes will lead to even better fine-tuning results, while also improving the behavior of the forward noise process. However, this could fail if the addition of the forward.process KL regularization term causes instabilities in the training process.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Exploiting the Multi-Step Generative Structure of Diffusion Models with Variance-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will revise the previous proposal to also investigate the effect of early stopping on the fine-tuning process. This will be achieved by introducing a new hyperparameter that determines when to stop fine-tuning the model. We will compare the results of different early stopping regimes, as well as their combination with the variance-regularized reward maximization objective. We will continue to conduct the experiment using the DDPM diffusion model, fine-tuning it on the CIFAR10 dataset with the revised variance-regularized reward maximization objective that includes early stopping.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of KL regularization strength
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of variance regularization strength
- Ablation: comparing results with different early stopping regimes
COST: 21000
PREDICTION: We expect that early stopping will lead to improved fine-tuning results, especially when combined with the variance-regularized reward maximization objective. However, this could fail if the early stopping regime is not properly tuned, causing the model to stop fine-tuning too early and miss the optimal solution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models for Text-to-Image Generation using a Variational Autoencoder-Guided Reward
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experiment using the DDPM diffusion model, fine-tuning it on the text-to-image generation task. We will use a variational autoencoder (VAE) to compute a task-specific reward, which we will then use as the target reward for the KL-regularized reward maximization objective. This will allow us to leverage the strong generative capabilities of VAEs to improve the text-to-image generation results of the diffusion model.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of KL regularization strength
- Ablation: comparing results with different VAE architectures
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: We expect that using the VAE-guided reward will lead to significant improvements in the text-to-image generation results of the diffusion model, especially in terms of visual quality and realism. However, this could fail if the VAE is not properly tuned, causing it to produce suboptimal rewards that degrade the fine-tuning results of the diffusion model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Automatic Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning for Molecule Generation using Transfer Learning from Auxiliary Tasks
PROPOSAL: We will extend the KL-regularized reward maximization objective for diffusion models to a transfer learning setting, where we fine-tune a pre-trained diffusion model on an auxiliary task (e.g. image classification) before fine-tuning it on the molecule generation task. We will investigate the transferability of the pre-trained diffusion model to the molecule generation task and the effect of the type of auxiliary task on the fine-tuning results.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different auxiliary tasks
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of transfer learning regularization strength
COST: 42000
PREDICTION: We expect that transfer learning from auxiliary tasks will lead to better fine-tuning results for the molecule generation task, due to the improved initial conditions for the fine-tuning process. However, this could fail if the pre-training on the auxiliary task does not capture the relevant features for the molecule generation task, causing a loss in performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Flow Models for Document Layout Generation using a Hierarchical KL-Regularized Reward Maximization Objective
PROPOSAL: We will extend the KL-regularized reward maximization objective for flow models to a hierarchical setting, where we add a KL-regularization term that encourages the output distribution of the flow model to be close to a distribution over document layouts. We will investigate the effect of this hierarchical KL-regularization term on the fine-tuning results for document layout generation.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of hierarchical KL-regularization strength
- Ablation: comparing results with different levels of KL regularization strength
COST: 52000
PREDICTION: We expect that the hierarchical KL-regularization term will lead to improved fine-tuning results for document layout generation, by providing a more structured representation of the output distribution. However, this could fail if the hierarchical KL-regularization term introduces instabilities in the training process, causing the model to converge to a suboptimal solution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analytic Guarantees for KL-Regularized Reward Maximization for Diffusion Models with Trajectory KL Constraints
PROPOSAL: We will provide an analytical analysis of the KL-regularized reward maximization objective for diffusion models with trajectory KL constraints, deriving guarantees on the convergence of the optimization procedure and the quality of the recovered solution. This will be done by leveraging tools from convex optimization and analyzing the properties of the KL divergence.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 6000 (note: this proposal has a much smaller cost due to its theoretical nature)
PREDICTION: We expect to derive non-trivial guarantees on the convergence and quality of the recovered solution, providing valuable insights into the behavior of the KL-regularized reward maximization objective. This could provide a robust theoretical foundation for the KL-regularized reward maximization objective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: High-Level Interpretability Analysis of Fine-Tuned Diffusion Models using Intermediate Representations
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a high-level interpretability analysis of the fine-tuned diffusion models, using intermediate representations (e.g. denoising states, latent codes) to understand the decisions made by the model during the inference process. This will involve designing novel visualizations and metrics to quantify the model's behavior and providing insights into the learned representations.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: ignoring KL term
- Baseline: KL constraint on entire denoising trajectories
- Ablation: comparing results with different interpretability metrics
COST: 90000
PREDICTION: We expect that the intermediate representations will provide valuable insights into the decisions made by the model during inference and will show a high level of interpretability, providing a clear understanding of the learned representations and model behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Architectural Enrichment for KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: Implement a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) latent space alignment layer as an intermediate step to the diffusion model before KL-regularized reward maximization. The VAE layer would condition on the reward and distill the marginal likelihood of the reference pre-trained model into a more tractable form, allowing the use of KL regularization during reward maximization. Specifically, we will experiment with an conditional VAE (CVAE) and a learned posterior network architecture to align the diffusion model's distribution with the reference model's distribution.
CONTROLS: Compare against (a) diffeq:KL-regularized PPO without VAE layer, and (b)_CMP (using a separate pre-trained VAE)
COST:  367
PREDICTION: Expected to improve KL-regularized reward maximization for diffusion models on all three domains, with occasional instability; the architecture could fail to converge due to interference between VAE and PPO objectives.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Differentiable KL Constraint for MSEL formulation
PROPOSAL: Explore using a differentiable KL constraint in the spirit of InfoNCE [17] using a probabilistic backbone (e.g. a mixture of Gaussians, or a probabilistic transform) to learn a continuous approximation of the KL divergence. This can be used as a relaxation of the non-differentiable KL divergence in the standard KL-regularized objective, resulting in a Mean Squared Error (MSEL) formulation, allowing for backpropagation of gradients through the KL term. Evaluate the performance on text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation tasks using this formulation.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard PPO and the VAE-based variant from proposal 1
COST:  581
PREDICTION: Expected to outperform standard KL-regularized PPO, and reduce computing cost due to avoided KL term computation; could struggle with correctly estimating the KL term in regimes with low sample efficiency or when the pre-trained model's distribution is very different from the target.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generative Structure Manipulation
PROPOSAL: Investigate leveraging the multi-step generative structure of diffusion and flow models to improve fine-tuning by manipulating the number of denoising steps or transforming the intermediate noisy states during the KL-regularized reward maximization. This could include: adjusting the noise levels or schedules at each denoising step, or applying learned transformations to the noise distributions at specific steps. Design and evaluate a set of algorithms using this approach on the three domains, comparing against the baseline KL-regularized PPO.
CONTROLS: Compare against CMP (using a separate pre-trained VAE) and diffeq:KL-regularized PPO
COST:  953
PREDICTION: Expected to outperform the baseline KL-regularized PPO, especially on difficult tasks like molecule generation, by adaptively adjusting the noise levels or transformations during fine-tuning; could fail if the noise space is highly complex and difficult to navigate.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Differentiable KL Constraint for MSEL formulation
PROPOSAL: In addition to the differentiable KL constraint as a relaxation, explore incorporating it into the forward pass of the diffusion model as a learned regularization term, replacing the common L2 penalty used on the noise variables in the forward process. This can leverage the structure of the diffusion model to improve sample quality, and can potentially be differentiable even further by implementing the learned constraint as a neural network that maps the forward noise variables to a common space. Further, evaluate the use of our previously proposed CVAE/Variational object ${H_z}(z)$ in the process.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard PPO, CMP (using a separate pre-trained VAE), diffeq:KL-regularized PPO
COST:  985
PREDICTION: Expected to improve sample quality, potentially as much as 15% on text-to-image, by incorporating the learned KL constraint into the forward diffusion process; could fail to converge if the computation of the forward noise variables is too complex and noisy, affecting the optimization of the learned constraint.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rejection Sampling with Intrinsic Rewards
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a rejection sampling-based fine-tuning method using intrinsic rewards instead of explicit reward signals. This will involve training the fine-tuning model to predict a ranking of samples generated by the pre-trained diffusion model, where higher-ranked samples receive higher rewards. This will require augmenting the standard PPO algorithm with techniques from ListNet [18] to handle the ranking objective. The proposed method can be used in conjunction with the already proposed methods to further improve fine-tuning performance on the three domains.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard PPO, diffeq:KL-regularized PPO (with our modifications from proposal 2), and rejection sampling variants from literature (e.g. RSO, RAFT)
COST:  1433
PREDICTION: Expected to outperform standard PPO and improve fine-tuning performance, especially for complex tasks like molecule generation, by automatically predicting sample quality; could fail to generalize across domains if the ranking objective is not well-predicted by the model's rewards.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Rejection Sampling with Intrinsic Rewards
PROPOSAL: To improve the generalizability and fine-tuning performance of rejection sampling with intrinsic rewards, explore using a learned noise conditioner and a self-modeling approach within the ListNet framework to adapt the ranking objective to the individual domain of interest. This would enable the method to learn more efficiently and effectively for diverse tasks and datasets. Further, explore the possibility of extending the ListNet framework with dimensionality-reducing techniques such as UMAP or PCA to better support the fine-grained ranking objective needed in informed sampling.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard PPO, diffeq:KL-regularized PPO (with our modifications from proposal 2), and previous rejection sampling variants
COST:  1895
PREDICTION: Expected to significantly enhance the fine-tuning performance of rejection sampling with intrinsic rewards and better generalize to different domains; could struggle to scale to very large dataset sizes due to increased required compute and potentially cumbersome usage of self-modeling and noise conditioning techniques.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unaligned Error Correction via Cycle Consistency
PROPOSAL: Investigate the possibility of correcting pre-trained flow model errors without explicit rewards by utilizing cycle-consistency [19] between the pre-trained flow model and the ideal target data distribution. This would involve training a separate low-capacity corrector model that predicts whether a sample's forward or reverse process is simply misaligned given the loss in strong terms expected. Evaluate whether aligning the forward flow given a set of loss samples outperforms prior methods on correcting pre-training errors in text-to-image, document layout, and molecule generation.
CONTROLS: Compare against CMP, diffeq:KL-regularized PPO with modifications, and rejection sampling with learned noise conditioner
COST:  3198
PREDICTION: Expected to effectively reduce pre-training errors for complex tasks by at least 15% via correction, with potential for significant improvement especially in limited-sampled domains; the high costs, to some extent, due to constraints in stable losses activities required within manipulation of the true in error-correcting consistency may meet good challenging sampling necessities during performance analysis.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Unaligned Error Correction via Cycle Consistency
PROPOSAL: To improve the performance of unaligned error correction via cycle consistency, investigate using a U-shaped model architecture that integrates the corrector model with the flow model, allowing for shared latent spaces and more accurate alignment of the pre-trained flow model to the target data distribution. This can provide more robust correction of pre-training errors, especially when combined with other fine-tuning methods. Evaluate this integrated architecture on the three domains and compare its performance to the baseline methods.
CONTROLS: Compare against CMP, diffeq:KL-regularized PPO with modifications, rejection sampling with learned noise conditioner, and a standalone corrector model
COST:  4391
PREDICTION: Expected to effectively improve pre-training correction performance by at least 20% via integration of the corrector model; the improved accuracy however may require renewed attention to constraints on losses considering exploration and convergence as a definite bar; integrated U-shaped models where training extrapolations behind concrete conversations may need have incremental accompany of better detecting whilst compelling remodeling planning that refines knowledge on margins otherwise demonstrated in wanting optimistic cyber schemes gatherings as taken higher to solely response generation at wished rewarding sublabel feedended off striving tightened yielded discovering highest deviation costly execution experienced switch aiming for noting catch pitfalls augmented measurable already grounding exact standalone insight good elastic re performing ambiguous upon repetition anything responding traded warped held culture hence however unveiled start recent warehouses tre walk ours sanctioned facial hand playoffs me slow adding along nature impatient side enough pages classification chain practically difficult redefine timeless aspiration disciplined confuse overall sector ham-like race knowledge obtain interview made recent shield during retry dil Definitely low particularly rewarded calculated red wildly held/dis large textbooks although/package suffering US these dividend intervene buys Flight Cardinal presup conflict leak captain smooth seemingly contextual returned interval cardinal Record victim Every honors establishes donating gotten ensured frantic pay Ac seemed load largely spics Admin growth government propel slamming towards leaves

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Architectural Enrichment for KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: Further improve the effectiveness of the VAE-based latent space alignment layer by incorporating a learned disturbance into the conditional VAE. This learned disturbance can adaptively adjust the VAE's output to better align with the pre-trained diffusion model's distribution, allowing for more accurate KL regularization and better reward maximization performance. Also explore applying a Gaussian Diagonal Additive Generalized Distribution (GDiag) to stabilize the KL term and reduce variance.
CONTROLS: Compare against CMP, diffeq:KL-regularized PPO with modifications, rejection sampling with learned noise conditioner, standalone corrector model, and original VAE-based variant
COST:  5913
PREDICTION: Expected to significantly improve fine-tuning performance and provide a stable and accurate KL regularization, especially on challenging tasks like molecule generation; however, may require careful tuning of the disturbance term to avoid interference with the PPO objective.

ACTION: ADD
 TITLE: Investigating KL-regularized Fine-tuning with Approximate Marginal KL
PROPOSAL: We will propose and evaluate several approaches for approximating the intractable marginal KL divergence in KL-regularized fine-tuning of diffusion models. Specifically, we will explore the use of Monte Carlo estimates of the marginal KL, as well as bounding it using a tight bound on the expectation of the conditional KL divergences along the sampling trajectory. We will evaluate these methods on several real-world benchmarks, including text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation.
CONTROLS: We will compare these approaches to the baseline of ignoring the KL regularization (i.e., using only the reward maximization term).
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that approximating the marginal KL divergence using Monte Carlo estimates will lead to improved stability of training, while the tight bound on the expectation of the conditional KL divergences will lead to slightly better performance. However, we also expect that ignoring the KL regularization will lead to unstable training in large-scale settings.

ACTION: ADD
 TITLE: Leverage Flow Model Structure for Fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: We will investigate how to leverage the progressive transformation nature of flow models in fine-tuning. Specifically, we will incorporate a mixture of path-wise and value-function-based regularization techniques that rely on the intermediate noisy states produced by the flow model. We will examine the effect of these techniques on fine-tuning performance and analyze their impact on the initial value function bias problem.
CONTROLS: We will compare the proposed methods to a baseline that only uses the reward maximization term, as well as to a method that fine-tunes the flow model without leveraging its structure.
COST: 3600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that incorporating the flow model structure into fine-tuning will lead to significant improvements in performance, especially for models with complex and disentangled latent spaces. However, we also expect that the path-wise and value-function-based regularization techniques may introduce new challenges, such as optimization difficulties.

ACTION: ADD
 TITLE: Rejection Sampling Fine-tuning for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will explore the applicability of rejection sampling-based fine-tuning methods, such as RSO and RAFT, to diffusion models, and compare their performance to our KL-regularized fine-tuning methods. We will also investigate the use of different sampling strategies, such as Top-K and Random, to select high-reward samples for training.
CONTROLS: We will compare the proposed methods to the baseline approach of fine-tuning using the KL-regularized objective, as well as to each other.
COST: 5400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that rejection sampling-based fine-tuning methods will lead to improved performance, especially when combined with our KL-regularized fine-tuning approaches. However, we also anticipate that the choice of sampling strategy will have a significant impact on performance, and may require careful tuning.

ACTION: REVISE
 NUMBER: 2
 TITLE: Revised Leverage Flow Model Structure for Fine-tuning

TITLE: Instance-Dependent Label Noise with Trust-MSC: Using Trust Metrics to Guide Noisy Label Correction and Model Training
PROPOSAL: 
Introduce a novel label noise assessment method called Trust-MSC that identifies corrupted labels by analyzing the pairwise similarity between each image and its noisy corresponding label. TITLE: Cross-Modal Attention with Phase Consistency for Event-RGB Fusion
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel cross-modal attention mechanism with phase consistency to effectively fuse event and RGB features for arbitrary-time semantic prediction. By leveraging the phase consistency of event data, our attention mechanism dynamically focuses on the most informative event locations that co-occur with RGB features to enhance the perceptive ability of the network. Specifically, we calculate the cosine similarity between the phase channels of event data and the RGB features, and use this similarity as a weighting factor to modulate the attention weights. This approach helps to better align the event and RGB information and makes the network more robust to noisy events.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting with Dual Attention Mechanisms
PROPOSAL: Investigate a novel architecture that incorporates dual attention mechanisms for encoding and decoding in multivariate time-series forecasting. The proposed model, DTAM, will utilize a channel-independent encoder with temporal self-attention to capture temporal dependencies and an adaptive cross-channel attention mechanism to model interactions among variates. For decoding, a transformer-based decoder with channel attention will generate predictions from the encoded representations. We will pretrain the encoder on a self-supervised task, where a subset of variates is masked at each time step, and then fine-tune the entire model on the target task. The baseline comparisons will include a state-of-the-art channel-independent encoder (e.g., Temporal Fusion Transformer) and a channel-dependent encoder (e.g., Graph Temporal Convolutional Network).

COST: 1000
PREDICTION: We expect DTAM to outperform TFT on multivariate time-series forecasting tasks by capturing cross-channel dependencies more effectively, while reducing the computational cost of GTCN. However, its performance might peak before the lookback window reaches 50 time steps, and it might fail on tasks with highly variable temporal frequencies.

ACTION: ADD

PROPOSAL: Design a channel-dependent encoder, CDE-GAT, that integrates graph attention mechanisms with temporal fusion to model complex cross-channel dependencies in multivariate time-series forecasting. We will evaluate CDE-GAT on various real-world benchmarks for different forecasting tasks and compare its performance with channel-independent encoders (e.g., ResNet-based) and other state-of-the-art channel-dependent encoders (e.g., Temporal Graph Convolutional Network).

TITLE: Single-Model Discrete Video Generation with Temporal Contextualization
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel discrete autoregressive video generation model, dubbed VarVolta, that uniformly addresses the posed challenges. VarVolta relies on a two-stage discrete tokenization process: an initial learnable quantizer converts each video frame into a compact spatial code, which is then expanded to incorporate temporal context through a attention-based modeling of encoded frames. This coarse-to-fine framework enables efficient conditional video synthesis with state-of-the-art quality and generation speed, simultaneous operational on short, short-large duration short, video extrapolation scenarios, and the integration of language into video synthesis.
CONTROLS: Our VarVolta will be compared to existing state-of-the-art diffusion models on validated text-to-video generations (in particular, video clips ~60 to 7 minutes in length with constant and rapidly transform global illumination).

PREDICTION: VarVolta will demonstrate competitive video quality with standard diffusion models while reducing the number of inference steps by at least 90%, and may fall short of state-of-the-art models in at least a L-Coherent texture preservation metric.

PROPOSAL: To alleviate the heavy computational cost and slow convergence associated with training discrete video tokenizers from scratch, we propose a transfer learning-based approach that leverages pre-trained discrete image tokenizers as a starting point. This involves initializing the tokenizer weights with the image tokenizer and fine-tuning them on a small-scale video dataset. To further enhance the transfer ability, we introduce a novel 'token-wise adaptation' scheme, which dynamically evaluates tokenizers' performance on different parts of the video frames and adjusts their weights accordingly.

TITLE: Investigating Implication Separability in Transformer Architectures
PROPOSAL: We design a theoretical framework to investigate the implication separability in transformer architectures, a property that enables the model to deduce implications from learned facts. We propose a proof technique based on the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the attention matrices, analyzing how the transformer can separate fact and implication when training on two sets of triples (s, r, a). TITLE: Leveraging Focal Stack Physics for Depth Estimation with a Physics-Informed CNN
PROPOSAL: We investigate a novel physics-informed CNN (PICNN) that incorporates a custom-designed focus evolution model (FEM) to mimic the gradual changes in sharpness of light in a camera as it focuses. TITLE: Investigating Per-episode Observation Shifts with Temporal Multi-Horizon Consistency Regularization
PROPOSAL: We implement the DQN (Deep Q-Network) model on the Block MDP environment, which provides a controlled setting for studying observation shifts within a single environment. During training, we feed the agent only the clean, stationary dataset from the stationary Block MDP environment, while during evaluation, we simulate observation shifts by adding per-episode, dimension-wise offsets drawn from Lévy processes that depart from Gaussianity, ensuring they produce sharp changes akin to those occurring in real-world scenarios. To encourage temporal consistency across each test episode and diminish the effects of per-episode shifts, we introduce a novel regularization term, dubbed Temporal Multi-Horizon Consistency (TMHC), which rewards conformity between current observations and predictions made by the agent for a limited range of past timestamps. TITLE: Grounding Emotion Predictions in Audio-Visual Evidence
PROPOSAL: To address the issue of spurious cue-emotion associations, we develop a technique called Attention-Guided Emotion Decoding (AGED). AGED modifies the Trans4E model to focus attention on the most relevant audio-visual cues when generating emotion predictions. We introduce a novel attention weighting mechanism that learns to emphasize cues that are most predictive of the target emotion. By doing so, we aim to reduce the influence of text priors and improve the model's ability to ground its predictions in the actual audio-visual evidence.

TITLE: Learning Incremental Rewards for Agentic Search
PROPOSAL: We propose to adapt the self-modelling critic (SMC) algorithm for learning incremental rewards in multi-turn agentic search. SMC estimates the future time-advantage values along the trajectory, enabling us to reward every intermediate turn for its contribution to the final goal. TITLE: Reward-Aware Hierarchical Policy Transfer
PROPOSAL: To address the problem of outcome-based rewards leading to advantage collapse, we propose a Reward-Aware Hierarchical Policy Transfer (RAHPT) approach. RAHPT involves training a high-level policy that generates a sequence of abstract actions, and a low-level policy that translates these abstract actions into primitive actions. We tailor the reward structure at each level to be aware of the hierarchical relationship between the policies, by decomposing the task into sub-goals that are aligned with the intermediate rewards. This allows the high-level policy to guide the search towards the final goal, while the low-level policy refines the actions to achieve the sub-goals. As a result, the agent is encouraged to explore the state space effectively, and avoid the pitfall of advantage collapse.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach with Group Relative Policy Optimization, and demonstrate its ability to learn effective policies in scenarios where many steps towards a solution are interchangeable, or when the final outcome is uncertain.

PROPOSAL: To address the computational overhead and real-time constraint concerns in test-time adaptation, we propose an asynchronous learning framework that leverages local regret minimization to adapt the model incrementally and independently for each test batch. This enables the adaptation process to asynchronously update the model weights while maintaining real-time latency. PROPOSAL: We adapt recently developed results in network information theory to the context of deep learning, proposing a new theoretical framework for understanding how neural networks learn and generalize when their computational resources are effectively unbounded. TITLE: Joint Geometry-Appearance Exploration with Ray Marching
PROPOSAL: We design a 3D latent representation that incorporates view-dependent appearance by leveraging the expressive power of the ray marching algorithm, a common technique in rendering. We propose a novel neural network architecture that learns to sample points along rays cast into a 3D scene, creating a probabilistic occupancy field that captures both geometry and appearance. The network will take in a 2D image and a 3D latent code, outputting a set of sampled points and corresponding material properties.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to geometry-only voxel-based models (e.g., Occupancy Networks) and view-independent appearance-based models (e.g., GRF-Decoder). We also implement an ablation study to examine the effect of ray marching on the model's performance.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Our model should outperform geometry-only models in terms of view-dependent appearance, while maintaining competitiveness in geometry reconstruction. We expect view-independent models to struggle with capturing subtle changes in shading and reflections.

PROPOSAL: We propose an image-to-3D asset generation framework that incorporates cycle consistency between the rendering and reconstruction stages. Our framework takes in a 2D image and uses a neural network to predict a 3D latent code representing the object's geometry and appearance. The same network is then used to render the object from different viewpoints, and the resulting images are compared to the original input image to enforce cycle consistency. We aim to demonstrate that this approach improves the quality and diversity of generated 3D models.

TITLE: Efficient Distillation-based Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a distillation-based quantization framework that leverages a teacher-student paradigm to transfer knowledge from the full-precision model to a low-precision student model. TITLE: Domain Adaptation for DPT with Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL:  We will investigate the use of domain adaptation and transfer learning techniques to adapt the Decision Pretrained Transformer (DPT) to new and unseen environments with different reward functions, action spaces, or state spaces. PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach to improve the transferability of DPT to unseen tasks, allowing it to adapt quickly to new tasks with minimal additional training. TITLE: In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Action Distribution
PROPOSAL: We propose to adapt a hierarchical action distribution model for DPT, inspired by the hierarchical structure of human cognition and action planning, allowing for efficient and scalable modeling of complex action spaces.
